parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This file sits in the domain layer, and its main job is domain work: an X-ray business rule that checks whether money is too concentrated in one account. evaluate() adds up each account's investment, finds the largest account, works out its share of the total and compares that share with the user's thresholdMax. getSettings() turns user preferences into rule settings, including the default threshold of 0.5. Both are domain logic.

There is no persistence, transport or framework logic here. Account from @prisma/client is used only as a type (Pick<Account, 'name'>). Nothing is stored or fetched, and no HTTP or framework code runs. Building the localized messages is handed off to the injected I18nService, so the file never builds UI strings itself. The explanation message is reasonably part of what a rule evaluation returns. Two small things lean toward presentation: getConfiguration() includes UI hints (step 0.01, unit '%'), and evaluate() formats the percentage with toPrecision(3). Neither is enough to say a whole responsibility has been put in the wrong layer.

Whether this file should depend on services from the application layer is an import-direction question, which is out of scope. I'm only moderately confident because the localization and UI-hint parts are a judgment call.
